Identity assessment: supplied source begins with OSF download provenance, title USING ELICITED IMITATION TO MEASURE GLOBAL ORAL PROFICIENCY IN SLA RESEARCH: A CLOSE REPLICATION STUDY, and authors Kevin McManus and Yingying Liu. It is labelled Preprint version, Language Teaching, accepted for publication 19 March 2020. Title, authors, journal, year and original-study identity match the neutral replication reference. Full primary research report with methods, results, references and appendices; not an abstract or secondary report. DOI is not printed in this candidate, so DOI identity is not independently confirmed. No PDF was supplied. Unassigned sides/fields are null placeholders only; not re-extracted. Target ambiguous; no positive statistic assigned. Printed candidates: overall item-mean syllable correlation r=-0.87, p<0.001, R2=0.76 (pp.21–22); group correlations Beginner r=-0.82, p<0.001, R2=0.67; Low r=-0.85, p<0.001, R2=0.72; High r=-0.87, p<0.001, R2=0.75 (p.22). Joint regression prints F(2, 27)=50.97, p<.001, R2=79.1 exactly as printed (p.23); do not convert 79.1 or infer eta-squared. Table 7 gives Coefficient (standardisation not specified): syllable length -0.18, SE 0.02, t=-8.83, p<0.001; attributive-clause presence -0.29, SE 0.14, t=-2.13, p=0.04. The item 11 versus 12 comparison prints Cohen’s d=0.78 [0.42,1.14] (p.22), without a same-comparison p there. No eta-squared is printed for these item-feature analyses. Requested metric alone cannot identify one of these tests; no effect conversion performed.
